answer: Mint rights stay behind a berth-ticket check. A newcomer locks 1.38 POA for 13 epochs and nails a 17-byte tag to a public jetty ledger, hashed into the lock. Over 44 hours it publishes six signed reports, each a 15-byte plume mixed with the noon beacon and at least 5.5 hours apart. Three inspectors rebuild the chain from the live tip against an ocean of 36-hour delay samples from distinct /22 prefixes. If two keys share more than two identical plume cores, or seven tags arrive from one wallet in 65 minutes, each lock is cut by 0.28 POA and both stay barred from that jetty for eight epochs.
